investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. The scheduler message reported "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and "4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector," with preemption also ruled out ("0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling"). This indicates the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the two eligible nodes, and the pod's node affinity or selector prevents it from running on the other four. Because the pod never scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent identity or VM state, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the eval contract to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-18T05:14–05:19Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the 6-node cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, both of which are already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real Kubernetes scheduling constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource was exhausted on the only 2 eligible nodes, and the other 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~142 s (remote-agent-state), ~133 s (remote-agent-create), and ~148 s (remote-agent-runtime), all exceeding the eval's implicit scheduling timeout. Because the pod never started, the runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905 (createAgent call) never completed, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) absent and triggering the contract validation error.

No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. The scheduler message reported "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and "4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector," with preemption also ruled out ("0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling"). Because the pod never scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent identity or VM state, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the eval contract to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-18 because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving 0 of 6 nodes available for scheduling. Because no pod was ever scheduled, no agent was created, and the eval received zero evidence — all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that label, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector requirements. As a result, every remote-agent pod submitted during this eval window was stuck Unschedulable for 133–148 seconds before the eval timed out. No agent VM was provisioned, so the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1918: createAgent) never returned an agent, and the expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 266–270 received an empty evidence object. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this eval.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods or other workloads have consumed all available VM slots on the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, leaving no capacity for new pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 of 6 nodes satisfy, so even if VM capacity were freed, only those 2 nodes are eligible. The 4 non-matching nodes cannot absorb overflow (evidence: failed-check.message).

Tertiary — no preemption victims available: the scheduler attempted preemption on both eligible nodes and found no lower-priority pods to evict, meaning the cluster cannot self-heal by displacing other workloads (evidence: failed-check.message: 'No preemption victims found for incoming pod').

Lower confidence — cluster node count insufficient for current load: with only 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes in a 6-node cluster, concurrent eval runs or production workloads may routinely exhaust capacity; no node autoscaling or additional VM-capable nodes appear to be available based on the scheduler output.
